You take part in QUARE Phase 2, a dialectical negotiation among five quality-specialized
agents (SafetyAgent, EfficiencyAgent, GreenAgent, TrustworthinessAgent, ResponsibilityAgent)
about the initial requirements of a software project. The negotiation runs in rounds; in each
round every agent speaks once and sees everything said before. Each turn follows the dialectical
structure: defend your thesis (your own requirements), raise antitheses (critiques of other
agents' requirements that undermine your quality dimension) and propose syntheses (merges,
decompositions, relaxed thresholds) that satisfy several constraints at once.

Conflict types: "resource" (qualities compete for finite resources, e.g. redundancy vs. energy),
"logical" (requirements impose mutually exclusive system states) or "redundant" (same intent).

Rules: refer to requirements only by their IDs; be concrete; keep "statement" under 120 words.
Always answer with a single JSON object with this schema:
{"statement": "your argument",
 "conflicts_raised": [{"ids": ["ID", "ID"], "type": "resource|logical|redundant", "description": "..."}],
 "positions": [{"id": "ID", "stance": "support|oppose|modify", "proposal": "change you propose or empty"}],
 "concessions": ["IDs of your OWN requirements you agree to relax or drop"],
 "agree_to_close": true or false}
Set "agree_to_close" to true only if you have no remaining objections.

PROJECT: Library - Library Management System

PROJECT DESCRIPTION:
A library management system must allow library members to borrow and return books. The system must track which books are available, which are borrowed, and by whom. Members must be able to search for books by title, author, or ISBN. The system must enforce borrowing limits (e.g., maximum number of books per member) and track overdue books. Librarians must be able to add new books, remove books, and manage member accounts.

INITIAL REQUIREMENTS (Phase 1):
[SafetyAgent]
SAF-01 (operational): The system shall ensure that no member can borrow more than 5 books simultaneously.
SAF-02 (tactical): The system shall automatically track and notify members of overdue books within 24 hours of the due date.
SAF-03 (tactical): The system shall maintain real-time inventory status of all books to prevent double borrowing.
SAF-04 (strategic): The system shall provide a backup mechanism to recover all transaction data in case of a failure.
SAF-05 (tactical): The system shall allow librarians to revoke borrowing privileges for members with outstanding overdue books.
SAF-06 (operational): The system shall implement a user authentication process to ensure only registered members can access borrowing features.
SAF-07 (tactical): The system shall log all transactions, including borrow and return actions, for audit purposes.
[EfficiencyAgent]
EFF-01 (tactical): The system shall enable searching for books with a response time of under 2 seconds for 95% of queries.
EFF-02 (operational): The system shall allow up to 10 simultaneous book borrow operations per member to optimize resource utilization.
EFF-03 (tactical): The system shall track book availability and update the status in real-time to ensure accurate information.
EFF-04 (operational): The system shall process book returns within 1 second to maintain high throughput.
EFF-05 (operational): The system shall send overdue notifications to members within 24 hours of the due date to ensure accountability.
EFF-06 (tactical): The system shall enable librarians to add or remove books with a latency of less than 3 seconds per operation.
EFF-07 (strategic): The system shall maintain an uptime of 99.5% to ensure consistent availability for users.
[GreenAgent]
GRN-01 (strategic): The library management system shall minimize energy consumption by using energy-efficient servers and infrastructure.
GRN-02 (tactical): The system shall provide an energy usage report for library operations at least quarterly.
GRN-03 (operational): The library management system shall enable digital notifications for overdue books to reduce paper waste.
GRN-04 (tactical): The system shall allow members to check the carbon footprint of each book based on its lifecycle impact.
GRN-05 (operational): The library management system shall implement a recycling program for damaged books, ensuring proper disposal.
GRN-06 (tactical): The system shall track the total energy savings achieved through digital operations compared to traditional methods.
GRN-07 (strategic): The library management system shall prioritize the acquisition of e-books to reduce physical resource consumption.
[TrustworthinessAgent]
TRU-01 (tactical): The system shall ensure that only authenticated members can borrow or return books.
TRU-02 (operational): The system shall log all borrowing transactions for auditability purposes.
TRU-03 (strategic): The system shall enforce data encryption for all member personal information stored.
TRU-04 (tactical): The system shall implement role-based access control for librarians and members.
TRU-05 (operational): The system shall provide a mechanism to report and manage overdue books securely.
TRU-06 (operational): The system shall allow members to update their personal information securely.
TRU-07 (tactical): The system shall require strong password policies for member accounts.
[ResponsibilityAgent]
RES-01 (tactical): The system shall ensure compliance with data protection regulations by implementing encryption for all member data.
RES-02 (tactical): The system shall provide an accessible interface for all users, including those with disabilities, to promote fairness and inclusivity.
RES-03 (operational): The system shall log all user actions related to book borrowing and returning for accountability.
RES-04 (operational): The system shall adhere to library borrowing policies by enforcing a maximum of 5 books per member.
RES-05 (tactical): The system shall automatically notify members of overdue books via email to promote responsibility.
RES-06 (strategic): The system shall implement a feedback mechanism for members to report issues or suggestions regarding fairness in library services.
RES-07 (strategic): The system shall provide an annual report on usage statistics to ensure transparency in library operations.

NEGOTIATION TRANSCRIPT SO FAR:
[Round 1] EfficiencyAgent: The EfficiencyAgent emphasizes the importance of performance efficiency in the library management system. Requirements EFF-01, EFF-02, EFF-04, and EFF-06 ensure that the system operates with low latency and high throughput, which is crucial for user satisfaction. EFF-03 guarantees real-time updates on book availability, enhancing user experience. However, I raise concerns about SAF-02 and RES-05, which may introduce delays in notifying members about overdue books, conflicting with our goal of maintaining a response time under 2 seconds for queries.
{"conflicts_raised": [{"ids": ["SAF-02", "RES-05"], "type": "logical", "description": "Overdue notifications may delay system responsiveness, conflicting with EFF-01 and EFF-04."}], "positions": [{"id": "SAF-02", "stance": "oppose", "proposal": "Modify to ensure notifications do not impact system performance."}, {"id": "RES-05", "stance": "oppose", "proposal": "Modify to ensure notifications do not impact system performance."}], "concessions": [], "agree_to_close": false}

[Round 1] GreenAgent: The GreenAgent emphasizes the necessity of sustainability in the library management system. Requirements GRN-01, GRN-03, and GRN-07 focus on minimizing energy consumption and promoting digital solutions to reduce waste. GRN-02 and GRN-06 ensure accountability and track energy savings, while GRN-05 addresses responsible disposal of damaged books. However, I raise concerns about EFF-02, which allows up to 10 simultaneous borrow operations per member, potentially increasing energy consumption and resource strain, conflicting with our sustainability goals.
{"conflicts_raised": [{"ids": ["EFF-02"], "type": "resource", "description": "Allowing 10 simultaneous borrow operations may increase energy consumption, conflicting with GRN-01."}], "positions": [{"id": "EFF-02", "stance": "oppose", "proposal": "Modify to limit simultaneous borrow operations to align with sustainability goals."}], "concessions": [], "agree_to_close": false}

[Round 1] SafetyAgent: The SafetyAgent emphasizes the critical importance of safety and reliability in the library management system. Requirements SAF-01 and SAF-04 ensure that borrowing limits and data recovery mechanisms are in place to prevent misuse and data loss. SAF-02 and SAF-05 are essential for notifying members about overdue books and revoking privileges, promoting responsible borrowing. SAF-03 guarantees real-time inventory status to prevent double borrowing, enhancing safety. However, I raise concerns about EFF-02, which may compromise safety by allowing excessive simultaneous borrow operations, increasing the risk of errors and misuse.

[Round 1] TrustworthinessAgent: The TrustworthinessAgent emphasizes the necessity of security and privacy in the library management system. Requirements TRU-01 and TRU-03 ensure that only authenticated members can access borrowing features and that personal information is encrypted, safeguarding user data. TRU-02 and TRU-05 promote auditability and accountability by logging transactions and managing overdue books securely. TRU-04 establishes role-based access control, enhancing security. However, I raise concerns about SAF-05, which may conflict with TRU-05 by potentially exposing sensitive information when revoking borrowing privileges. Additionally, EFF-01's response time requirement may hinder the implementation of robust security measures, impacting TRU-01 and TRU-03.

[Round 1] ResponsibilityAgent: The ResponsibilityAgent emphasizes the importance of ethical compliance and accountability in the library management system. Requirements RES-01 and RES-02 ensure data protection and accessibility for all users, promoting fairness. RES-03 and RES-04 enforce accountability by logging user actions and limiting borrowing to 5 books, respectively. RES-05 ensures members are notified of overdue books, fostering responsibility. RES-06 and RES-07 enhance transparency and allow for feedback. However, I raise concerns about EFF-02, which may compromise fairness by allowing excessive simultaneous borrow operations, conflicting with RES-04. Additionally, SAF-05 may expose sensitive information during privilege revocation, conflicting with RES-01.
{"conflicts_raised": [{"ids": ["EFF-02"], "type": "logical", "description": "Allowing 10 simultaneous borrow operations may conflict with the maximum borrowing limit, undermining accountability."}, {"ids": ["SAF-05"], "type": "logical", "description": "Revoking borrowing privileges may expose sensitive information, conflicting with data protection regulations."}], "positions": [{"id": "EFF-02", "stance": "oppose", "proposal": "Modify to limit simultaneous borrow operations to align with accountability goals."}, {"id": "SAF-05", "stance": "oppose", "proposal": "Modify to ensure secure handling of sensitive information during privilege revocation."}], "concessions": [], "agree_to_close": false}

[Round 2] EfficiencyAgent: I appreciate the concerns raised by other agents regarding performance efficiency. However, I maintain that EFF-02 is crucial for optimizing resource utilization. To address the conflicts, I propose modifying EFF-02 to allow up to 8 simultaneous borrow operations instead of 10, balancing efficiency with safety and responsibility. Additionally, I suggest that overdue notifications (SAF-02 and RES-05) can be streamlined to ensure they do not impact system performance, allowing for timely alerts without compromising response times.

[Round 2] GreenAgent: I appreciate the EfficiencyAgent's proposal to limit simultaneous borrow operations to 8, which is a step towards balancing efficiency with sustainability. However, I still oppose EFF-02 as allowing any more than 5 simultaneous borrow operations could significantly increase energy consumption. I propose modifying EFF-02 to allow a maximum of 5 simultaneous borrow operations to align with our sustainability goals. Additionally, I support the idea of streamlining overdue notifications (SAF-02 and RES-05) to minimize resource usage while maintaining accountability. This can help reduce energy consumption associated with notification processes.

[Round 2] SafetyAgent: I appreciate the proposals from the EfficiencyAgent and GreenAgent regarding simultaneous borrow operations and overdue notifications. However, I maintain that safety must be prioritized. Allowing up to 8 simultaneous borrow operations (EFF-02) still poses a risk of errors and misuse, which conflicts with SAF-01. I propose a synthesis: modify EFF-02 to allow a maximum of 5 simultaneous borrow operations, ensuring safety while still optimizing efficiency. I support the streamlining of overdue notifications (SAF-02 and RES-05) to minimize performance impact, as long as it does not compromise timely alerts.

Your own requirements are RES-01, RES-02, RES-03, RES-04, RES-05, RES-06, RES-07. This is round 2 of at most 3.
Respond to what the other agents said: hold, concede or propose syntheses.
Answer with the JSON object only.
